_meta.indication: Radioactive diagnostic agent indicated for Positron Emission Tomography (PET) imaging of the brain to estimate β-amyloid neuritic plaque density in adult patients with cognitive impairment who are being evaluated for Alzheimer's Disease (AD) and other causes of cognitive decline.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 14595 - Pivotal 'Histopathology' Study (also referenced as Study A in labeling)
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, non-randomized study comparing florbetaben F18 PET imaging to postmortem histopathology (standard of truth based on Bielschowsky Silver Staining per CERAD criteria with immunohistochemistry) in terminally ill subjects who consented to post-mortem brain examination.
pivotal_trials.population: Safety population of 216 subjects including 137 with Alzheimer's Disease, 31 with other dementia, 5 with Dementia with Lewy Body, 32 non-demented volunteers, and 11 young healthy volunteers; images from 82 autopsied subjects were interpreted against the subject-level histopathology standard of truth.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints of sensitivity and specificity of visual assessment of florbetaben F18 PET compared to histopathology standard of truth; prespecified sensitivity threshold 0.6 and specificity threshold 0.5, with the lower 95% CI limit required to exceed these thresholds for at least 3 of 5 blinded readers.
pivotal_trials.n: Images from 205 subjects evaluated; 82 autopsied subjects interpreted against subject-level histopathology standard of truth.
pivotal_trials.result: Study met co-primary endpoints: 3 of 5 readers achieved prespecified sensitivity and specificity thresholds, so the combined null hypotheses were rejected. In labeling (in-person training readers), median sensitivity was 98% (range 96-98) and median specificity 80% (range 77-83).

key_safety: No serious adverse reactions related to Neuraceq administration were reported. The most commonly reported adverse reactions were injection site reactions: pain (3.9%), erythema (1.7%), and irritation (1.2%). Safety is based on 978 administrations to 872 subjects.
target_moa: Florbetaben F18 is an F18-labeled stilbene derivative that binds to β-amyloid plaques in the brain; after IV administration it crosses the blood brain barrier and shows differential retention in brain regions containing β-amyloid deposits, and the F18 isotope produces a positron signal detected by a PET scanner.
modality: Radiopharmaceutical (F18-labeled stilbene derivative small-molecule PET imaging agent).

rems.type: A REMS is not necessary; the main safety concern is radiation risk and the Division agreed a REMS is not needed to manage the risk.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary and there were no controversial issues that would benefit from discussion.

description.text: Removed limitations of use and added indication for selection of patients indicated for amyloid beta-directed therapy; added quantitative image analysis

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for changes to the INDICATIONS AND USAGE section of the prescribing information by removing the limitations of use and adding a new indication, specifically, use for selection of patients who are indicated for amyloid beta-directed therapy as described in the prescribing information of the therapeutic products. In addition, the use of quantitative image analysis is added to the Image Display and Interpretation subsection of the DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION section.

summary.text: Neuraceq (florbetaben F18) was a 505(b)(1) new molecular entity NDA given standard review. Approval was based on a pivotal Phase 3 histopathology study (14595) comparing PET visual assessment to postmortem histopathology; after a complete response was anticipated, the applicant submitted new confirmatory reader data as a major amendment, the PDUFA date was extended, and the NDA was approved without a REMS or postmarketing requirements.

citations.quote: On December 21, 2012 Piramal Imaging SA submitted an original 505(b)(1) New Drug Application (NDA 204677) for Neuraceq (florbetaben F 18 injection).

basis.text: A complete response action was anticipated due to inadequate efficacy data in the initial NDA submission, but instead the applicant submitted a major amendment with new confirmatory data and the application was approved without an actual CRL being issued.

citations.quote: A complete response action for the application was anticipated because the efficacy data in the initial NDA submission were not adequate to establish the effectiveness of florbetaben F 18 as an amyloid imaging agent.
